jobs.description: Employer: Watermark Donut Company Expires: 09/19/2026 Job Title: Institutional Growth & AI Outreach Intern for Boston’s premier Dunkin’ Franchise.Role: Develop a proprietary institutional catering business, focusing on businesses, hospitals and schools in our footprint.Company: Watermark Donut Company, LLC- 22 Boston Locations plus 2 Cambridge and 1 Charlestown.Corporate Office: 100 Grossman Drive Suite 307 Braintree, MA 02184; accessible via Red line.Time Commitment: Part-Time (15-20 hours/week) | Flexible around class schedulesCompensation: Competitive Hourly Base + Performance-Based Commission KickerAbout UsWatermark Donut Company, LLC runs a high-volume portfolio of 25 Dunkin’ locations strategically clustered throughout Downtown Boston, the Seaport, Cambridge, Charlestown and major medical hubs (MGH, Tufts, Longwood Medical, and Boston Medical Center). We are launching an innovative, tech-forward push to develop a B2B Catering Business. We are looking for a sharp, autonomous student to help us build our direct sales pipeline.The RoleThis is not a "coffee delivery" internship. You will be working directly with our leadership as well as Dunkin’s corporate team to build a modern B2B sales engine from scratch. Your mission is to develop a network of institutional catering customers in areas proximate to our stores. You will leverage cutting-edge AI prospecting tools to identify, message, and close corporate partnerships with tech firms, professional offices, pharma reps, educational institutions, and hospital floor managers.Key ResponsibilitiesAI-Powered Prospecting: Utilize generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude) and sales databases to automate and personalize hyper-local B2B outreach. Objective is to identify key contacts and then deploy smart "bounce-back" campaigns to add corporate customers to our platform.Targeted Local Networking: Coordinate with ezCater to facilitate deliveries. Develop an AI-driven email outreach program targeting potential catering customers in areas proximate to our stores.Account Optimization: Ensure our menu interfaces are optimized for corporate “Bundles" and bulk-order options.What We Are Looking ForThe Hustle: A current student (BU, BC, Northeastern, Suffolk, or similar) studying Business, Hospitality, Tech, or Entrepreneurship.Tech Fluency: You already use AI tools to accelerate your workflow and know how to prompt effectively for professional copywriting and data sorting.Local Navigation: You know the layout of our markets.Autonomy: You love a role where you aren't micro-managed. You view the hundreds of potential catering customers near our stores as a portfolio of opportunities to mine.What's In It For You?Real-World AI & B2B Experience: Build a real sales funnel on your resume using modern tech tools.Flexible Hours: We will completely work around your class schedule.Financial Upside: A solid hourly base rate protects your time, but a commission kicker on new account revenue means your earning potential is directly tied to growth in catering.Physical Demands and Working ConditionsWork is primarily performed in a professional office environment, with periodic local travel to Watermark Donut Company store locations, prospective customer sites, meetings, and other business locations throughout the Greater Boston area. Travel may involve driving, walking, or public transportation. The position requires prolonged computer and telephone use, as well as occasional standing, walking, bending, reaching, climbing stairs, and carrying business-related materials weighing up to approximately 25 pounds. Store and customer visits may involve exposure to varying weather conditions and typical retail and food-service environments.Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) StatementWatermark Donut Company, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.description: Employer: Wash Naturals Expires: 09/19/2026 Wash Naturals is a Boston-based body scrub brand that turned a boring bathroom step into a social moment. We’re known for our interactive retail experience, cult-favorite hand & body scrubs, and a brand voice that doesn’t sound like anything else in skincare. You’re the face of Wash Naturals at Faneuil Hall. Offer hand scrub samples at our branded sink station, walk people through the experience, pitch the product, and close the sale.Content Creation — Make It Look Good. Film and edit short-form video for our social channels. Set up and conduct mini mic interviews. Capture raw in-store content. Post to Wash Naturals socials as needed. Facilitate content creator program logistics.HOW TO APPLYWe don’t just want a resume. We want to see what you can create.Submit your resume, a short cover letter, and a short-form video you’ve shot and edited yourself. Grab any skincare product in your house and create a TikTok or Reel that shows how you’d capture and present it — keep it under 60 seconds. We want to see your eye, your editing style, and your energy. Email everything to: marisa@washnaturals.com

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Mars Snacking Finance Internship at Mars, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Mars, Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 At Mars, we work together to build a better world for people, pets, and the planet. From being a socially responsible business, to investing in our Associates, we're always looking at how we can make tomorrow brighter. As an Associate, you are empowered with the freedom and tools to be yourself, to forge your own path, to build relationships across our global community, to discover the right opportunities for you to grow – all with ample support. Here, you have our ongoing commitment to your growth and development as you work across our world-famous brands. Start your journey at Mars today! Mars Snacking Finance Internship Experience As a Mars Snacking Finance Intern, you will gain exposure to the following areas: Help our finance teams drive our digital agenda by unlocking analytics capabilities, processes and helping to mold the usage and adoption of next generation applications and technologies Collaborate with various stakeholders to drive value through tangible, project-based assignments (vary depending on business need) with visibility to senior leadership within the organization Build capability in sought after skills including but not limited to data storytelling, analysis, process optimization, senior leader communication, project ownership and stakeholder alignment A competitive experience with the potential to join full-time within the MARS Finance Leadership Experience (MFLE) program post-graduation after a successful internship and candidate evaluation. What we’re looking for: We are looking for agile students who have a drive for results, a desire to learn, and who can quickly build relationships We are looking for students who are passionate about the consumer products industry and are majoring in Finance, Accounting, or related business fields Eligible candidates will intern the summer prior to their final graduation date (typically rising seniors) Willingness to relocate to the site of the role Open to students legally authorized to work in the U.S., without the need for current or future work sponsorship Employment is contingent upon successful completion of drug & background screening Eligible candidates will be responsible for personal transportation to and from work site during duration of the internship program. What can you expect from Mars? The Mars Internship Experience is a 10-week summer program providing excellent depth of experience with real business problems and opportunities. Exciting professional and social engagement activities throughout the experience that provide opportunities to network with your intern peers all the way up to senior leaders. Best-in-class training and development from Day 1, including a formal mentor, access to our in-house Mars University, and more. Ongoing coaching and mentorship to help you succeed and get the most out of your experience. Some pretty sweet perks including competitive salary & benefits package, fun freebies, and pet-friendly offices. About Mars, Incorporated For more than a century, Mars, Incorporated has been driven by the belief that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. This idea is at the center of who we have always been as a global, family-owned business. Today, Mars is transforming, innovating, and evolving in ways that affirm our commitment to making a positive impact on the world around us. Across our diverse and expanding portfolio of Snacking, Food, and Petcare products and services, we employ over 140,000 dedicated Associates who are all moving in the same direction: forward. As a $65 billion family-owned business, we produce some of the world’s best-loved brands including ROYAL CANIN®, PEDIGREE®, WHISKAS®, CESAR®, M&M’S®, SNICKERS®, Pringles®, Cheez-It®, and BEN’S ORIGINAL™. and take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health and services businesses, including AniCura, Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, and VCA™. We know we can only be truly successful if our partners and the communities in which we operate prosper as well. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire our Associates to take action every day to help create a world tomorrow in which the planet, its people and pets can thrive. The Mars Compass, inspired by the Economics of Mutuality, is used to measure the company’s progress in service of its purpose; The world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. For more information about Mars, please visit mars.com. Join us on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube.

jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 Internship Program Overview The Polaris Engineering Internship is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. This program is for future leaders who seek a culture built on innovation, passion, and collaboration. As an Engineering Intern, you will be given impactful, project-based assignments that allow you to have exposure to multiple facets of engineering so you will experience both larger ongoing projects as well as shorter-scale projects throughout the summer that align with our business objectives. You will be placed into a specific team based on interest and business needs. These teams could include, but are not limited to: Design Engineering Project Engineering Systems Engineering Test or Development Engineering Potential Placement Locations Could Include: Roseau, MN; Wyoming, MN; Huntsville, AL; or San Angelo, TX, Novi, MI As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to and from the office. Required Qualifications: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master's degree in Engineering (e.g. mechanical, electrical, computer, software, or systems engineering) with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Able to complete full 12-week internship working 40 hours per week within the dates: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Previous Internship/Co-op experience Previous experience using CAD or equivalent software (Creo highly desired) Hands-on engineering experience through prior internship or clubs (ex. SAE, Clean Snow) This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.description: Employer: County of Orange - County of Orange Expires: 09/19/2026 Position Land Survey Paid Intern (Technical Intern)Deadline to ApplyPlease note the deadline for this recruitment is Wednesday, September 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM (PT). OC Public Works (OCPW) provides services on a regional basis to unincorporated areas, to cities, and to other County agencies and departments. The primary mission of the department is to protect and enrich the community through the sustainable delivery of projects and services. OC Public Works’ guiding principles are safety, integrity, quality, teamwork, and adaptability.OCPW is a unique County department comprised of ten (10) service areas: Administrative Services, Agricultural Commissioner/Sealer of Weights & Measures; OC Construction; OC Development Services; OC Environmental Resources; OC Facilities Design & Construction and CUF; OC Facilities Maintenance; OC Fleet Services; OC Infrastructure Programs; OC Operations & Maintenance.OC CONSTRUCTIONOC Construction provides project management and construction management services for projects on OC Public Works' Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and Maintenance Improvement Program (MIP) as well as OC Parks and other County department projects. OC Construction focuses on horizontal projects such as roads, bridges, bikeways, and flood control channels.For more information on OC Public Works click here.For more information on the County of Orange click here.THE OPPORTUNITYThe Land Survey Intern position provides students with valuable hands-on experience by working alongside licensed land surveyors and experienced professionals on a wide variety of public infrastructure projects throughout Orange County. Interns have the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge in a real-world setting while gaining exposure to both office and field surveying practices. Land Survey Interns will assist survey staff with a variety of office and field assignments.Land Survey Interns will assist survey staff with a variety of office and field assignments, including: Assisting with boundary, topographic, construction, hydrographic, and control surveys. Collecting field measurements using GNSS, total stations, digital levels, terrestrial laser scanners, and UAV technologies. Processing field data and assisting with drafting, mapping, and preparation of survey deliverables using CAD and survey software. Assisting with research of deeds, maps, survey records, right-of-way documents, and other legal records. Organizing project files, field notes, and digital records. Performing other related technical duties that support the Survey-Field Services unit while developing practical knowledge of professional land surveying practices. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSThis recruitment is open to applicants who are currently enrolled in or have graduated within the last six (6) months from an accredited college or university pursuing a degree or certificate in Land Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field. jobs.description: Employer: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital Expires: 09/20/2026 ** Please note, applications are not accepted through Handshake. Please see application portal information below. Applications through Handshake will not be considered.OverviewThe St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital Healthcare Administration Graduate Student Program is a cohort model internship experience designed to offer motivated graduate students the opportunity to spend a summer working in healthcare administration and operations. The cohort reports to both the Strategic Planning and Decision Support Office and the Office of the CAO/CFO. During the summer program, the selected students will gain an in-depth understanding of pediatric hospital and clinical operations, research operations, and administrative operations, with a focus on financial operations, campus operations, quality and patient safety, clinical logistics and space, internal audit, strategic planning, and innovation and design.Internship descriptionThe student will participate in financial, strategic, and operational projects that support the organization. Students should expect to be available Monday through Friday from 8:30 am until 5:00 pm, starting May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Final dates depend on the chosen students’ academic schedule. The internship will be 12 weeks long. The program is located in Memphis, TN, and requires relocation to the Memphis area. The internship is not designed to be a hybrid or remote opportunity. Compensation, housing, and parkingCompensation will be provided in a stipend format paid monthly. For students not local to the Memphis area, St. Jude will provide housing. It is paid for by St. Jude and offered at no cost to the student. Parking is free on campus. Other perks and benefits may apply. As of fall 2026, this monthly stipend amount is $2,946.00. St. Jude does not offer signing bonuses, moving expenses, or other reimbursements to stipend students. The stipend amount is subject to change and selected students will be notified of any updates. Qualifications and application processTo be considered, applicants must electronically submit the following items by Monday, October 19, 2026, 11:59 PM CST, to the application portal. After the deadline, applications and edits to applications will not be accepted. Please note, applications through Handshake are not accepted. Students must be currently enrolled in a graduate program and cannot have graduated prior to the start of the internship program.Cover letter in PDF format addressing an interest in healthcare administration and describing what the student seeks from the experience Those seeking degrees other than MHA should articulate how they’ll use this experience within their current graduate programCurrent, updated resume in PDF format Graduate transcript Unofficial, electronic copies are accepted Download links are not accepted Undergraduate transcripts may not be submitted in lieu of graduate transcripts First year students: Submit your transcripts even though they might not yet have grades. They will have earned the equivalent of their bachelor’s degree by May 2027They are currently enrolled in graduate-level coursework as of fall 2026Candidates whose applications are complete and meet the requirements will be reviewed by the program administration review committee. Candidates remaining under consideration will be asked to complete a phone screen. Those remaining under consideration after the phone screen will be invited to complete a virtual panel interview with St. Jude leaders. Offers will be extended from December 2026 – January 2027. All other applicants will be notified of their status by mid-January 2027. Unsolicited resumes to the program administration team are not accepted. All applications must be submitted through the application portal. Candidates will be evaluated on a variety of factors including education experience, leadership experience, and past work or internship experience, as well as how their goals and interests align with what St. Jude is able to offer the student cohort. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Forward Deployment Engineer at AppleOne Employment Services
jobs.description: Employer: AppleOne Employment Services Expires: 09/20/2026 About ActOne GroupActOne Group Industries builds and deploys AI agents and automations that run real business workflows for enterprise clients. Our platform, Foundry, lets teams design, build, and ship AI applications and agents — and we work side-by-side with clients to get those solutions into production. We're a small, fast-moving team where the work you do reaches customers quickly. About the RoleThis is a Forward Deployment Engineer (FDE) internship — but you don't need a traditional engineering background. You need sharp business instincts, genuine curiosity about AI, and the drive to learn how to build.Forward Deployment Engineers sit at the intersection of client and product. You'll learn how to translate a client's business problems into working AI agents and applications, build them on Foundry using Claude Code, and help clients do the same. A big part of the summer is helping us design and build a client training program — alongside our AI Lead — that teaches customers how to build their own AI applications and agents from scratch.If you've been the person who picks up new tools fast, builds things on the side, and likes being in the room with customers, this is for you. Why This Is an Exciting OpportunityThe way work gets done is being rewritten right now, and Forward Deployment Engineers are the people doing the rewriting. You won't be watching the AI shift from the sidelines — you'll be on the front line of it, sitting with real businesses and turning "what if AI could do this?" into something that's actually running in production.This is a rare chance to get genuinely fluent in the tools and workflows that will define the next decade of work, while you're still early. You'll build real AI agents and applications, shape how clients learn to build their own, and develop a skill set very few people have yet: knowing how to take AI from a demo to deployed value. The people who learn this now — how to think with these tools, sell with them, and ship with them — are the ones who will be leading teams and companies in a few years. We're betting that's you. What You'll DoWork directly with clients to understand their workflows, goals, and where AI can create real valueLearn to build AI agents and applications on the Foundry platform using Claude CodeHelp design and build our client-facing training program alongside the AI Lead — the curriculum that teaches clients how to build and deploy their own AI solutionsSupport client onboarding and the hands-on deployment of solutionsGet deep, practical exposure to the leading AI tools — Claude, OpenAI, and the broader stack — and develop strong judgment about when and how to use eachDocument patterns, write clear guides, and turn what works into repeatable playbooks Who You AreStrong business fundamentals — you understand how companies actually operate and make decisionsHands-on AI exposure — you've used tools like Claude and OpenAI extensively, ideally building real things with them, not just experimentingA fast, self-directed learner — comfortable with ambiguity and figuring things out without a manualA clear communicator — you can hold your own in a client conversation and explain technical ideas in plain termsPrior startup or technology experience (required) — you've worked at a startup or tech company, founded something, or built and shipped your own product. You know what it's like to move fast in an environment without a playbook.Currently enrolled in a college or university program Bonus PointsA portfolio of AI projects you've built — apps, agents, automations, prompts, anythingFamiliarity with no-code/low-code tools or prompt engineeringExperience in a client-facing, sales, or consulting setting The DetailsLocation: Los Angeles, CA — hybrid (mix of in-person and remote)Duration: SemesterCompensation: Discussed during the interview processGrowth: Strong interns will be considered for a full-time offer after the summer

jobs.title: Project Management Intern at Oaklin Lane
jobs.description: Employer: Oaklin Lane Expires: 09/22/2026 Project Management Intern — The Pediatric CollectiveLocation: RemotePosition Type: InternshipSchedule: Part-time during the academic year or full-time during the summerCompensation: PaidAbout The Pediatric CollectiveThe Pediatric Collective is an industry association. It brings together pediatric therapy companies, clinicians, parents, caregivers, researchers, and other industry leaders committed to improving access to high-quality care for children.Pediatric therapy does not receive enough attention despite the enormous need. Families often face long waitlists for speech, occupational, physical, and behavioral therapy—in some communities, children may wait months or even years for an appointment. These delays can cause children to miss critical opportunities for early intervention.The Pediatric Collective was created to help change that. We plan to elevate pediatric therapy as a national priority, increase awareness of the challenges facing children and families, share promising practices across the industry, and bring together organizations that can help develop meaningful solutions.The Pediatric Collective is separate from Oaklin Lane and is intended to represent and include companies throughout the pediatric therapy industry.To learn more, visit:https://www.linkedin.com/company/tpcollective/About the RoleWe are looking for an organized, resourceful, and mission-driven Project Management Intern to help build The Pediatric Collective and coordinate initiatives designed to advance the pediatric therapy field.You will help turn ambitious ideas into well-executed projects. This may include organizing industry working groups, coordinating research and educational initiatives, developing events, managing content projects, and bringing together stakeholders from across the pediatric therapy community.This is not an observational internship. You will own meaningful workstreams, collaborate with industry leaders, and help build an association with the potential to improve access to care for children and families nationwide.What You’ll DoDepending on your interests and experience, projects may include:Developing project plans, timelines, milestones, and success measuresCoordinating initiatives involving therapy providers, clinicians, parents, researchers, and industry partnersOrganizing meetings, working groups, webinars, roundtables, and other eventsTracking responsibilities, deadlines, risks, and follow-up items across multiple projectsSupporting research into therapy access, waitlists, workforce shortages, reimbursement, and other industry challengesHelping develop reports, educational resources, and industry recommendationsCoordinating content and communications for The Pediatric CollectiveIdentifying and engaging potential association members and partnersResearching organizations and leaders that could contribute to the Collective’s missionDocumenting processes and building systems that allow initiatives to scalePreparing presentations, project updates, and materials for industry leadersPresenting recommendations directly to The Pediatric Collective’s leadershipWho Should ApplyWe welcome undergraduate and graduate students from all academic backgrounds, including:Project or program managementBusiness or entrepreneurshipHealthcare administrationPublic healthPublic policyPsychology or child developmentEducation or special educationCommunicationsSpeech-language pathologyOccupational or physical therapyOther related disciplinesPrior healthcare or project-management experience is not required. We care more about initiative, organization, communication, and a genuine interest in improving access to pediatric therapy.Strong candidates will be:Passionate about helping children and familiesHighly organized and attentive to detailComfortable managing multiple priorities and deadlinesStrong writers and communicatorsSkilled at coordinating people with different perspectivesAble to bring structure to open-ended projectsComfortable working independently in a remote environmentProactive, dependable, and eager to take ownershipWhat You’ll GainOwnership of high-impact projects within a developing national industry associationExperience coordinating initiatives involving companies, clinicians, families, and other industry leadersDirect exposure to the challenges facing pediatric therapy providers and the families they serveOpportunities to build relationships across healthcare, therapy, research, and public policyExperience developing scalable project-management systems and processesDirect interaction with The Pediatric Collective’s leadershipThe opportunity to help elevate pediatric therapy as a national priorityHow to ApplyPlease submit your application through The Pediatric Collective LinkedIn page:https://www.linkedin.com/company/tpcollective/Candidates should include a resume and a short explanation of why they are interested in helping The Pediatric Collective advance pediatric therapy and improve access to care for children and families.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Strategy & Operations Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/24/2026 Strategy & Operations Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the Founders Office, working directly with the COO on the problems that decide whether the firm wins: strategy, hiring, product, and the operating machinery underneath all of it. Read the whole post before applying.This is not an internship where you watch. You'll sit in the rooms where decisions get made, then own pieces of what comes out of them. One week that's building the model behind a pricing decision, the next it's running point on a search for a senior hire, the next it's turning a half-formed product idea into a spec someone can build. Real deadlines, real consequences, with someone experienced beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the firm actually works, and earns the right to own bigger and bigger pieces of it.You'll doStrategy and analysisBuild the analyses behind real decisions: pricing changes, new service lines, pod capacity, which states and specialties to push into next.Pull data out of our systems, clean it, and turn it into a one-pager the COO can decide from. Numbers first, narrative second.Research competitors, markets, and tax industry shifts, and tell us what actually matters instead of dumping links.Pressure-test plans before they ship. Find the assumption that breaks, and say so.RecruitmentRun searches end to end for roles across the firm: write the post, source candidates, screen against our rubrics, schedule, keep the pipeline moving, and make sure no candidate is left hanging.Sit in on interviews, take structured notes, and build the debrief materials that drive the hire or no-hire call.Keep the Monday recruiting board clean and the funnel numbers honest.Product and internal toolingTurn dictated voice notes and whiteboard sessions into written specs, task lists, and process docs that an engineer or ops person can execute against.Test what gets built. Find where it breaks, document it precisely, and chase the fix until it closes.Help design and roll out the AI and automation workflows the firm runs on, so the team's reps go to judgment, not busywork.Founders Office operationsPrep leadership meetings: agenda, prior action items, the two or three numbers needed to run it.Capture action items out of leadership and pod meetings and chase them until they close, including with people more senior than you.Run special projects nobody owns yet: an offsite, a new vendor evaluation, a fire that landed on the COO's desk this morning.Draft communications the COO sends under their own name. They should need edits, not rewrites.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program, and we mean that literally, because we require a 3.9+ overall GPA to apply. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Thinking. You can take an ambiguous question, structure it, do the work, and come back with a recommendation and the reasoning behind it. Not a summary of the problem. An answer.Communication. You write clean, professional messages and documents that people can act on without a rewrite. You follow up without being asked. You don't go quiet when something is stuck.Ownership and discretion. You'll see strategy before it's announced, comp, and personnel matters. That information does not leave your hands. When something is yours, it gets done or you raise your hand early. Nothing dies silently in your queue.And be honest with yourself about the unglamorous work. Founders Office means you do whatever the firm needs, and some of it is scheduling, data cleanup, and chasing people for the same document three times. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If work below your ego drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: you'll prepare the analysis and the options. Decisions with real legal or financial exposure belong to the COO and the founders. You will never be left holding those alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time in the Founders Office, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.RequirementsGraduating May 2027 or later.Minimum 3.9 overall GPA. We will verify. If you're below it, please don't apply.Pursuing a degree in business, finance, accounting, economics, or a related program. Exceptional candidates from other fields will be considered.Strong written communication. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Comfortable in spreadsheets, fast with new software, and already using AI tools in your own work.Discretion with confidential information, without needing to be reminded.Hungry to earn a full-time seat and own it.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Growth Intern (Content / Social Media / Community) at Pinnie Health
jobs.description: Employer: Pinnie Health Expires: 09/24/2026 Pinnie Health | New York, NY | Part-Time / Internship About Pinnie HealthMillions of older adults in America are failed by healthcare every day. They get discharged from the hospital with no follow-up plan. They miss medications because nobody explained the instructions. They give up trying to fight a denied insurance claim. They don't know what they're entitled to, and there's nobody helping them figure it out. The system wasn't built for them, it was built around them.Pinnie Health exists to fix that. We're building the first AI-powered care advocacy platform that gives every older adult on Medicare a dedicated human advocate, backed by AI that handles the research, coordination, and follow-up, at zero cost to the patient. We launched three months ago, we've already enrolled over 100 patients, we're licensed in 46 states, and we're growing fast. This is early-stage, high-impact work at the intersection of healthcare and technology, and we're just getting started. The RoleWe're looking for someone who understands how to build a social media presence from nothing. Someone who's already grown accounts on Instagram, Facebook, or both, and can prove it. You'll be our first dedicated social media hire. The job is building Pinnie's organic presence across Instagram and Facebook from scratch: daily content using a mix of AI-generated visuals, static graphics, patient testimonials, short-form video, articles, community posts, and whatever formats you think will connect with our audience. You'll also help manage a UGC agency we're working with to produce creator content around elder care and Medicare. The people you'll be making content for are older adults navigating Medicare, dealing with denied claims, trying to find a doctor who actually listens. The audience is their families, their caregivers, and the patients themselves. There are 67 million people on Medicare in this country, and almost nobody is making good content for them. That's the opportunity. We're not handing you a content calendar and asking you to execute. We want someone entrepreneurial who will come in, take ownership, and treat this like their own brand. You'll work directly with both founders, you'll have budget to spend, and you'll have the freedom to move fast. If you prove you can grow it, this becomes a full-time role. What You'll DoBuild and run our Instagram and Facebook. Create and publish content daily across both platforms. Static posts, carousels, Reels, Stories, testimonials, AI-generated imagery, quote cards, articles, community discussion posts. You'll figure out what formats work on each platform and double down on what gets traction. Use AI tools to move fast. You're comfortable with tools like Midjourney, ChatGPT, Higgsfield, or whatever's new this week. You use them to produce more and better content, not as a crutch. Grow an organic community. Build a following of Medicare beneficiaries, their adult children, and caregivers who actually engage. We care about people who click through and sign up, not vanity follower counts. Figure out what content sparks conversation and sharing in this audience. Manage our UGC agency. We're working with a UGC agency to produce creator content. You'll be the point person: reviewing briefs, giving feedback on deliverables, making sure the output fits our brand and actually performs. Experiment constantly. Test hooks, formats, posting times, hashtag strategies, content series. Track what works. Kill what doesn't. Bring us ideas we haven't thought of. Why PinnieYou'll build a brand for a massive underserved audience. 67 million Medicare beneficiaries. Their adult children. Their caregivers. Nobody is making great social content for this population. You get to own that space. We'll give you real ownership. No approval chains, no brand police. If you have an idea, pitch it at standup and post it that afternoon. We're a small team that moves fast, and we'll back you if you show results. The content matters. This isn't promoting a lifestyle brand or selling SaaS. The stories you'll tell are about real people getting help they couldn't find anywhere else. Families find us through the content you'll create. It can turn into a career. This starts as a part-time role. If you grow the channels and prove you can own the function, we'll convert it to full-time. Who You AreYou've grown a social media account and can show the numbers. Yours, a brand's, a client's. We want to see the before and after.You think big and are entrepreneurial. We want to take big swings and build a massive brand to drive awareness about a service that matters. You post consistently. Not once a week. Daily or close to it. You understand that cadence is half the game.You're fluent in AI content tools. You already use them in your workflow and can show us what you've made with them.You have visual taste. Your feed doesn't look like a template dump. You know color, composition, and typography well enough to make things people want to share.You can write captions and short copy that sounds human, not like a brand account. No "we're thrilled to announce." Real voice.Based in or near NYC. Some in-person collaboration in our Tribeca office, but most of the work is remote. What You Don't NeedA marketing degreeAgency experienceA follower countWe care about what you can make, not what's on your resume. DetailsLocation: Remote (If in NYC, hybrid as needed in our Tribeca office)Hours: ~20 hrs/week, flexible scheduleCompensation: Hourly Paid Internship ($ based on experience)Duration: 3 months with potential to extend or convert How to Apply1. Please submit your resume on this job post.2. Please go to pinnie.com and spend some time understanding what we do and who we serve. Then email aashay@pinnie.com the following: a. An account you've grown. Include the handle and the numbers (where it started, where it is now, timeframe). b. A content plan. We're starting from zero on Instagram and Facebook. Pitch us 2-3 content series or recurring formats you'd launch in your first two weeks. Tell us why you think they'd work for this audience. c. One big idea. What would you do in the first 90 days to build a real community around Pinnie? We're not looking for a polished deck. A few paragraphs showing how you think is plenty. That's the whole application.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Founders Office Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/24/2026 Founders Office Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the Founders Office, working directly with the COO on the problems that decide whether the firm wins: strategy, hiring, product, and the operating machinery underneath all of it. Read the whole post before applying.This is not an internship where you watch. You'll sit in the rooms where decisions get made, then own pieces of what comes out of them. One week that's building the model behind a pricing decision, the next it's running point on a search for a senior hire, the next it's turning a half-formed product idea into a spec someone can build. Real deadlines, real consequences, with someone experienced beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the firm actually works, and earns the right to own bigger and bigger pieces of it.You'll doStrategy and analysisBuild the analyses behind real decisions: pricing changes, new service lines, pod capacity, which states and specialties to push into next.Pull data out of our systems, clean it, and turn it into a one-pager the COO can decide from. Numbers first, narrative second.Research competitors, markets, and tax industry shifts, and tell us what actually matters instead of dumping links.Pressure-test plans before they ship. Find the assumption that breaks, and say so.RecruitmentRun searches end to end for roles across the firm: write the post, source candidates, screen against our rubrics, schedule, keep the pipeline moving, and make sure no candidate is left hanging.Sit in on interviews, take structured notes, and build the debrief materials that drive the hire or no-hire call.Keep the Monday recruiting board clean and the funnel numbers honest.Product and internal toolingTurn dictated voice notes and whiteboard sessions into written specs, task lists, and process docs that an engineer or ops person can execute against.Test what gets built. Find where it breaks, document it precisely, and chase the fix until it closes.Help design and roll out the AI and automation workflows the firm runs on, so the team's reps go to judgment, not busywork.Founders Office operationsPrep leadership meetings: agenda, prior action items, the two or three numbers needed to run it.Capture action items out of leadership and pod meetings and chase them until they close, including with people more senior than you.Run special projects nobody owns yet: an offsite, a new vendor evaluation, a fire that landed on the COO's desk this morning.Draft communications the COO sends under their own name. They should need edits, not rewrites.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program, and we mean that literally, because we require a 3.9+ overall GPA to apply. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Thinking. You can take an ambiguous question, structure it, do the work, and come back with a recommendation and the reasoning behind it. Not a summary of the problem. An answer.Communication. You write clean, professional messages and documents that people can act on without a rewrite. You follow up without being asked. You don't go quiet when something is stuck.Ownership and discretion. You'll see strategy before it's announced, comp, and personnel matters. That information does not leave your hands. When something is yours, it gets done or you raise your hand early. Nothing dies silently in your queue.And be honest with yourself about the unglamorous work. Founders Office means you do whatever the firm needs, and some of it is scheduling, data cleanup, and chasing people for the same document three times. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If work below your ego drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: you'll prepare the analysis and the options. Decisions with real legal or financial exposure belong to the COO and the founders. You will never be left holding those alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time in the Founders Office, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.RequirementsGraduating May 2027 or later.Minimum 3.9 overall GPA. We will verify. If you're below it, please don't apply.Pursuing a degree in business, finance, accounting, economics, or a related program. Exceptional candidates from other fields will be considered.Strong written communication. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Comfortable in spreadsheets, fast with new software, and already using AI tools in your own work.Discretion with confidential information, without needing to be reminded.Hungry to earn a full-time seat and own it.

Business Development & Channel: Dealer Policies, Dealer Distribution Footprint, Key Market Performance Management, Showroom Display & Merchandising. Product Line Sales: Program Development & Execution, Demand/Supply Analytics, Competitive Analysis, Retail Critical Thinking Leadership. Field Sales: Dealership Experience, Retail Root Cause & Countermeasure, Dealer Operations Improvement, Solicitation Ownership, Sales Enablement. We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Plymouth, MN or Medina, MN. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to/from the office. Required Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s/master’s degree in business with an emphasis in Sales, Marketing, or other related degree with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Must be able to commit to a full 12-week internship, working 40 hours per week, within one of the following date ranges: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: 2027 Marketing Internship at Polaris Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 09/24/2026 Marketing Internship - Summer 2027 Company Overview Polaris Inc. is a global leader in powersports and known to millions of people around the world as we offer a diverse portfolio of products and services including boats, off-road vehicles, commercial vehicles, and more. Polaris pioneers’ product breakthroughs and enriching experiences and services, that have invited people to discover the joy of being outdoors since our founding in 1954. At Polaris, we have fun doing what we love by driving change and innovation. We empower employees to take on challenging assignments and roles with an elevated level of responsibility in our agile working environment. Our people make us who we are and help create incredible products and experiences that empower us to Think Outside. Internship Program Overview The Polaris Marketing Internship (MIP) is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging sophomores, juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. As a Marketing Intern, you will be given impactful project-based assignments that directly align with business objectives. These projects could include exposure, within our marketing division, across various segments including targeted development in these areas: Brand and Product Marketing (Brand/Lifestyle Marketing, Insights and Analytics) How you create and capture through brand and product marketing Creative and Content (Social Media, Paid Media, Partnerships, Events) How Creative and Content Creation drives business today and tomorrow Process and Go-to-Market (Ecommerce, Digital Production) How Process, Planning and communication improve work Dealer and Channel (Channel, Retail, Owner Experience, In-Market and Key Market Impact) How Dealership and Sales Channels impact our business We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Any Polaris location across the United States. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: you participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to/from the office. Required Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s/ master’s degree in Marketing, Strategic Communications, or other related business degree with an emphasis in Marketing with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Must be able to commit to a full 12-week internship, working 40 hours per week, within one of the following date ranges: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Previous Internship/Co-op experience or involvement in relevant projects. Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Strong Communication (both written and verbal including strong presentation skills) Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing, multi-tasking environment Strong organizational and project management skills This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!
